original_problem_statement: I want to build a system that automatically detects hate speech in social media comments using NLP. It should work in real time on a stream of comments and flag the toxic ones.
clarified_problem_statement: Build a real‑time system that ingests a stream of English‑language comments from the Twitter/X and Reddit APIs, uses a transformer‑based model (e.g., fine‑tuned BERT) to assess each comment for hate speech, and returns a JSON record containing the original text, a toxicity score (0–1), a categorical label (hate_speech, offensive, clean), a confidence score, and an explanation of why the comment was flagged. The system must handle ≥ 500 comments per second with ≤ 50 ms latency per comment on a single A100‑class GPU.
expected_input: A continuous stream of English text comments fetched via the Twitter/X and Reddit APIs.
expected_output: For each comment, a JSON object with fields: {"text": <original>, "toxicity_score": <0‑1>, "label": "hate_speech"|"offensive"|"clean", "confidence": <float>, "explanation": <human‑readable reason>}.
constraints: Throughput ≥ 500 comments/second; latency ≤ 50 ms per comment; single NVIDIA A100 GPU; English‑only input; must provide human‑readable explanation for flagged comments; no budget limits; standard API usage terms apply.
datasets_and_technologies: Primary dataset: Jigsaw Toxic Comment dataset (Kaggle). Model: transformer‑based (e.g., BERT) fine‑tuned for toxicity detection. Libraries: Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch or TensorFlow. Deployment: streaming from Twitter/X and Reddit APIs, inference on a single A100 GPU, possible use of fast tokenizers and accelerated inference (e.g., ONNX, TorchScript).
other_requirements: Explainability: system must produce a human‑readable rationale for each flagged comment (e.g., highlighted terms, attention scores, or generated text). No multilingual support required at this stage.
assumptions: No multilingual support needed; no specific regulatory or privacy constraints beyond typical API terms; unlimited budget; deployment environment can host a single A100 GPU; standard ML libraries (PyTorch/Hugging Face) are acceptable.
research_focus: Identify existing open‑source projects that implement real‑time hate‑speech detection with transformer models, and locate recent (last ~3 years) academic papers on high‑throughput toxicity classification and model explainability techniques suitable for real‑time deployment.
